result.journal: Proc. ACM Meas. Anal. Comput. Syst.
result.keywords: Hybrid query processing systems increasingly combine CPU and GPU resources to accelerate large-scale data workflows. This article studies adaptive filtering strategies for join processing when filter selectivity, execution overheads, and hardware placement vary across workloads. We examine how lightweight bloom-style filters can be co-processed with join operators, how stale or low-value filters affect throughput, and how performance changes on resource-constrained systems. Using measurements from representative analytical pipelines, we identify common cases where filtering improves latency but also cases where excessive filtering logic introduces dead weight and degrades execution efficiency. We propose an adaptive scheduler that selects when to apply GPU-assisted filters, preserving most of the speedup while reducing overhead on smaller machines. The approach is especially useful for mixed workload environments and distributed data platforms that must balance speed, energy use, and operator complexity.
result.title: Adaptive GPU-Accelerated Filtering for Join Processing in Crowdsourced Data Pipelines.
